'''''Arctium minus''''', commonly known as '''lesser burdock''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''little burdock''', '''louse-bur''', '''common burdock''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate = 2 January 2018}}</ref> '''button-bur''', '''cuckoo-button''',<ref name=GRIN/> or '''wild rhubarb''',<ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=ARMI2 USDA PLANTS information]</ref> is a [[biennial plant]] native to Europe.

== Description ==
''Arctium minus'' is a [[biennial plant]] growing up to {{Convert|1.8|m|ft|frac=2}} tall<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=Elias|first1=Thomas S.|title=Edible Wild Plants: A North American Field Guide to Over 200 Natural Foods|last2=Dykeman|first2=Peter A.|publisher=[[Sterling Publishing|Sterling]]|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4027-6715-9|location=New York|pages=112|oclc=244766414|orig-year=1982}}</ref><ref name="tfb">{{Cite book |last=Francis-Baker |first=Tiffany |title=Concise Foraging Guide |date=2021 |publisher=[[Bloomsbury Publishing|Bloomsbury]] |isbn=978-1-4729-8474-6 |series=[[The Wildlife Trusts]] |location=London |pages=80}}</ref> and form multiple branches. It is large and bushy. The [[leaves]] are up to {{Convert|50|cm|abbr=on}} long and ovate. The lower leaves are heart-shaped and have very wavy margins. Leaves are dark green above and woolly below. It grows an extremely deep taproot, up to {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} into the ground.<ref>John W. Thieret, William A. Niering, and Nancy C. Olmstead. ''National Audubon Society Field Guide to North American Wildflowers, Eastern Region, Revised edition''. Chanticleer Press, Inc, 2001. {{ISBN|0-375-40232-2}}</ref><ref>Richard H. Uva, Joseph C. Neal, and Joseph M. Ditomaso. ''Weeds of the Northeast''. Cornell University Press, 1997. {{ISBN|0-8014-8334-4}}</ref> The plant produces flowers in its second year of growth, from July to October. The flowers are prickly and pink to purple in color. The flower heads are about {{convert|2|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} wide, surrounded by a cluster of [[bracts]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="tfb" /> The outer bracts end in hooks causing a [[Hook-and-loop fastener|hook-and-loop]] effect after the flower head dries, when the bracts will attach to humans and animals to transport the seedhead.<ref name="The Wild Flower Key2">{{cite book |last=Rose |first=Francis |title=The Wild Flower Key |publisher=Frederick Warne & Co |year=1981 |isbn=0-7232-2419-6 |pages=386–387 |authorlink=Francis Rose}}</ref>

The flowers resemble and can be easily mistaken for thistles, but burdock can be distinguished by its extremely large leaves and its hooked bracts.

== Distribution and habitat ==
The plant is native to Europe,<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=arctium+minus Altervista Flora Italiana, Lappola bardana minore Arctium minus (Hill) Bernh.] includes photos plus European distribution map</ref> but has become introduced elsewhere such as [[Australia]], [[North America|North]] and [[South America]], and other places.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242416085 Flora of North America, Vol. 19, 20 and 21 Page 170 Common or lesser burdock, petite bardane, cibourroche, chou bourache, bourrier, ''Arctium minus'' (Hill) Bernhardi, Syst. Verz. 154. 1800. ]</ref><ref>[https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Arctium%20minus.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref>Marticorena, C. & M. Quezada. 1985. Catálogo de la Flora Vascular de Chile. Gayana, Botánica 42: 1–157</ref><ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/Arctium+minus Atlas of Living Australia]</ref>

== Uses ==
The leafstalks (up to a year old), leaves,<ref name="tfb" /> and flower stalks can be eaten raw or cooked. The roots are edible boiled with a change of water,<ref name=":0" /> though become too woody to eat in plants over a year old.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Benoliel|first=Doug|title=Northwest Foraging: The Classic Guide to Edible Plants of the Pacific Northwest|publisher=Skipstone|year=2011|isbn=978-1-59485-366-1|edition=Rev. and updated|location=Seattle, WA|pages=55|oclc=668195076}}</ref> The leaves can also be used to make [[herbal tea]].<ref name="tfb" />
